grading.scale: A+ 95-100, A 90-94, A- 85-89, B+ 80-84, middle cutoffs not in the excerpt, D listed as <55
grading.curve: No curve; absolute scale, so every student can earn an A.
grading.drop: Per the component table, 2 of 14 writing labs and 5 of 29 lecture-discussion sessions are dropped; no drops for essays, research paper or exams.
grading.extraCredit: Up to two optional extra credit essays worth 2% each (4% total), plus lecture-discussion quizzes worth up to 5% taken in class by app (4-5 of 5 correct = 2 points, 3 of 5 = 1 point, 1-2 of 5 = 0.5 poi

GLBL 280.finalExam: Length, time and location follow the official exam schedule.
GLBL 280.attendance: Weekly writing lab participation is graded and the lecture-discussion quizzes are taken in class; no further attendance rule in the excerpt.
GLBL 280.lateWork: Late papers are accepted only until 4 p.m. on the Friday of the week they were due, in both paper and electronic form, with a penalty (see Writing Assignments page for details). A missing paper draft
GLBL 280.makeups: Tell the TA in advance if an exam or work will be missed; conflict exams follow university policy on the Exam Information page.
other: Course total is 0.7 x writing component + 0.3 x exam component.
A student under 50% on the writing component may be given a failing grade in the course.
Grade questions must be raised within 1 week after a paper and within 2 weeks after an exam is returned.
Papers are scanned by plagiarism-detection software; AI use follows the separate AI policy page.
AI use must be disclosed with a standard statement at the end of each assignment; undisclosed use counts as academic dishonesty.
Students must document how they used AI and be ready to submit the full chat log as an appendix.
Citing hallucinated treaty clauses, fake studies or wrong technical data costs 15 points per occurrence; egregious cases may be reported as misconduct.
Work entirely homogenized by AI may be returned for revision or penalized; AI may not draft essays from scratch or generate figures.
